newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai central bank chief has quit - tv report.
newsitem.headline: Thai central bank chief has quit - tv report.

text.p: Bank of Thailand Governor Rerngchai Marakanond has submitted his resignation, local television station ITV reported on Monday.
The station's reporter, quoting sources close to Rerngchai, said the governor would not be going to work on Tuesday. It gave no further details.
No one was available at the central bank to confirm the news report.

Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh told reporters in northwestern Chiang Rai, where the cabinet is due to hold its weekly meeting tomorrow, that he would hold a news conference on the reported resignation of the governor on Tuesday.
He did not reply when asked by newsmen about the reported resignation, but simply nodded his head in response.
There have been market rumours in recent weeks that the governor was planning to resign, but such speculation has previously been denied by both Rerngchai and the authorities.

Earlier On Monday, Rerngchai told reporters that premier Chavalit and Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya had agreed in principle since July 22 to seek loans from the IMF to help rescue the country's ailing economy.

But although he confirmed Thailand was in talks with the IMF on ways to revive the economy, finance minister Thanong Bidaya took pains to say that any borrowing from the IMF was still being studied and a decision had not yet been taken.
Thailand's economy is going through its worst crisis in over a decade, and politicians fear IMF assistance may come with unpopular strings attached.

Last Friday, Rerngchai took the unusual step of defending his bank's decision to float the baht last month, saying it was made through established procedures and with the knowledge of Thanong and other finance ministry officials.
"The governor has never issued instructions or taken decisions contrary to proposals made by senior central bank officials. Any such accusations are therefore groundless," he said.
Rerngchai's statement was in response to Thai media reports that Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh had instructed the governor to float the baht.

"Some reports said the prime minister ordered the central bank governor to change the exchange rate system. But under legal and established prodecure...which can be verified, it is the governor who would make such proposal to the finance minister for his approval before it is forwarded to the prime minister," he said.
The baht has since fallen by more than 20 percent, sparking criticism that the central bank switched to the new system without proper consideration.
